concept.name: Percentile
concept.definition: The 100-quantiles of a distribution or ordered data set: the kth percentile is the value at or below which k percent of the observations fall. Percentiles express the relative standing of a value within a data set.
concept.intuition: Scoring in the 90th percentile means 90% of values are at or below yours and 10% above - a rank statement, not a statement about the score itself.
concept.mechanics: Order the data; for the kth percentile compute the rank index i = (k/100)(n + 1) - if i is an integer take that data value, otherwise average the two neighboring ordered values (other packages use different interpolation rules). Quartiles are the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles.
concept.formula: Index for the kth percentile: i = (k/100) * (n + 1), where n is the number of ordered observations; the percentile is the ith ordered value if i is integral, else the average of the two bracketing values (one common convention of several).
concept.failure_modes: Percentile values depend on the interpolation convention and are unstable in small samples, especially near the extremes. In non-stationary series, a percentile rank computed on one regime says little about standing in another.
concept.misconceptions: The 90th percentile does not mean scoring 90% - it is a statement of relative position. Nor is the difference between the 90th and 10th percentiles 'the middle 80% of values' by magnitude; it is by count.
concept.example: A fund's one-day return of -4% is worse than 99% of its historical daily returns, putting it at the 1st percentile - an extreme-tail day by its own history.
